title: Visiting Ancient Side as Restoration Continues: Routes, Hours and a Half-Day Plan
excerpt: Side's ruins now have new visitor routes, a reception area and two museums, but the great theatre is still closed. Here is how to plan a visit, especially in the cooler months.

body.text: Side, on a narrow peninsula in Antalya's Manavgat district, is one of the few places on the Turkish Riviera where a resort town and an ancient city share the same streets. GoTürkiye describes it as an open-air museum, with shops that have glass floors over the remains. In November 2026 Hürriyet Daily News reported, citing the excavation head, that a long restoration programme has now reached more than 40 locations across the site. That changes the visit in useful ways, but not everything has reopened. This guide explains what is new, what is still closed, and how to plan a half day or a full day around it.

According to [Hürriyet Daily News](https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/major-restoration-project-revives-40-ruins-in-side-229075) (6 November 2026), the work at Side is part of the ministry's Heritage for the Future programme, which started in November 2022. The excavation head, Prof. Feriştah Alanyalı, said that visitor reception facilities and sightseeing routes have been created, and that excavation, conservation and repair are complete on the major monuments along those routes. Work is continuing: excavation and landscaping on the land and sea walls, and restoration at the West Gate on the road to the East Gate.

Earlier in 2026, [Hürriyet Daily News](https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/side-debuts-museum-night-tour-routes-223795) reported an enlarged visitor area with new routes, a welcome centre and renewed streets, and the opening of a second museum, named after the archaeologist Arif Müfid Mansel, alongside the existing Side Museum. At the ancient harbour entrance, the Temple of Athena was partly re-erected, with several original columns reassembled, in work completed in November 2024, according to [Hürriyet Daily News](https://hurriyetdailynews.com/restored-athena-temple-emerges-as-key-landmark-in-side-ancient-city-206660); it stands beside the Temple of Apollo. We found no official hours or ticket details for the new museum, so ask at the welcome centre. In practice, this means a visitor in 2026 can follow a marked route rather than piecing the city together between hotels and car parks.

The Roman theatre is the building most people picture when they think of Side, and it is the one to check before you go. Both official museum portals, [the ministry's ticket site](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=SDO01&DistId=SDO) and the [Turkish Museums page for the site](https://www.turkishmuseums.com/museum/detail/1971-antalya-side-archeological-site/1971/4), currently list the theatre as closed for restoration; the latter gives the closure date as 29 November 2024. Even GoTürkiye's Side page still describes performances there, so treat that as background, not a programme. No reopening date had been announced when we checked. If seeing the inside of the theatre is the reason for your trip, wait for an official reopening notice.
Hours and tickets: what the official pages say

items: Ancient site: the ministry's ticket site lists 08:00–17:00 daily, with the ticket office closing at 16:30, and a foreign visitor ticket of €7. Note that the ministry lists this ticket under the name 'Side Theatre', and neither official page says which parts of the ancient city (such as the colonnaded street, the temples or the harbour) are inside the ticketed area, so ask at the ticket office what the ticket currently covers while the theatre is closed. The Turkish Museums page gives longer summer hours (until 21:30 from mid-March to 2 October, then until 19:30 for the rest of October) and does not list separate hours for November to mid-March, so plan on the shorter daytime schedule in winter.

Side Museum: the [Turkish Museums page for the museum](https://www.turkishmuseums.com/museum/detail/1959-antalya-side-museum/1959/4) gives winter hours (2 October–30 April) of 08:30–17:30 and a foreign adult ticket of €5. The ministry's [Side Museum page](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?sectionId=SDM01&distId=SDO) shows 08:30–19:00 (ticket office 18:30), and its page for the ancient site says the €7 site ticket is also valid for Side Museum entry. The two pages do not agree, so check at the ticket office whether one or two tickets are needed.

Night visits: Side has been part of the ministry's summer night museum programme, which [GZT](https://www.gzt.com/seyahat/gece-muzeciligi-2026da-20-muze-gece-acik-4237085) reported ran from 1 June to 1 October in 2026, with the site open until 22:00. The 2026 conditions published for night entry were aimed at MüzeKart holders, so check what applies to you. From November, plan only on daytime opening.

2027 prices: new ministry tariffs are scheduled to apply from 1 April 2027, according to fee schedules reported in September 2026. Our [2027 museum fees guide](/blog/turkiye-museum-site-fees-2027) explains what changes and how to budget.

body.text: A half-day route that works in winter

With the site closing in the late afternoon from November, the simplest plan is a morning start. Begin at the museum, because it gives context to the street plan and holds sculpture from the city; GoTürkiye notes that it occupies a former ancient bath. Then walk the main colonnaded street across the peninsula towards the temple area by the ancient harbour. GoTürkiye describes Side's grid layout, with a main boulevard running from the great gate to a square near the temples, which is still the easiest way to orient yourself. Finish at the harbour side for lunch. Allow two to three hours on foot, longer if you read every panel, and wear shoes with grip: ancient paving can be uneven and slippery after rain.

Use the new routes rather than cutting through work areas. The walls and the West Gate are active work zones, and following the marked paths is both safer and the best way to see the monuments that have already been restored.
Turning it into a full day

GoTürkiye places Side about 80 km east of Antalya city and 7 km southwest of Manavgat. The most natural pairing is Aspendos, whose Roman theatre GoTürkiye calls one of the best preserved of its kind; it puts the drive from Side at about 27 km, or around 40 minutes. The [Turkish Museums page for Aspendos](https://www.turkishmuseums.com/museum/detail/1963-antalya-aspendos-archaeological-site/1963/4) lists winter hours (1 November–30 April) of 08:00–17:00, with the ticket office closing at 16:30. A realistic winter day is Aspendos early, Side late morning and early afternoon, then back to your hotel before dark. Perge, another major ancient city of the region, is on the Antalya side of Aspendos and is usually easier to combine with a day based in Antalya city.

items: Check the ministry ticket site on the morning of your visit for hours and any closure notices.
Do not plan around the theatre interior until an official reopening is announced.
Ask what the site ticket covers while the theatre is closed, and whether the museum needs a separate ticket.
In winter, arrive before midday so you are not racing the 16:30 ticket cut-off.

If you are staying in Belek or Antalya, see our [Belek trip planner](/blog/belek-antalya-golf-trip-season-planning) for how Side fits a coastal stay, and our [Side destination page](/destinations/side) for the town itself.

body.text: Side rewards visitors who come with modest expectations about one building and big ones about the city as a whole. The restored streets and new routes make the ancient layout easier to read than it has been for years, and in the quieter months you may have long stretches of it largely to yourself.

seo.intent: Plan a visit to the ancient city of Side in 2026–27: what the restoration changed, what is closed, hours, tickets and how to combine it with Aspendos.
seo.uniqueValue: Reconciles the November 2026 restoration report with both official museum portals, flags the still-closed theatre and conflicting museum ticket rules, and turns them into a winter half-day route and a Side–Aspendos day plan.

quality.reviewNotes: Prepared 2026-11-10 from a research fact sheet. Independent EN fact check re-opened all cited sources (HDN 6 Nov 2026 and 29 Jun 2026, muze.gov.tr site and museum pages, turkishmuseums.com site/museum/Aspendos pages, three GoTürkiye pages) and required fixes were applied: Athena temple claim sourced to HDN Mar 2025 and placed at the harbour entrance; night-season dates attributed to GZT with the MüzeKart condition; muze.gov.tr museum page cited; ticket coverage hedged ('Side Theatre' ticket name, ask what it covers); October hours added; 2027 tariff wording softened; Perge sentence reworded; title changed to 'as restoration continues'. Official pages conflict on museum hours and ticket rules; the article shows both. No first-hand visit, Apollo temple status or theatre reopening date claimed. Independent translation review of DE/zh-CN/KO/ES with fixes applied (restored 'reported' hedges and GoTürkiye attribution, grammar). Not a human or native-speaker certification.
